executive_summary: Across the last six quarters, Northern Arc Capital has demonstrated a steady recovery and strengthening trajectory after FY25 stress, with AUM growth re-accelerating to 20%+ run-rate, improving ROA (2.4% → 2.7%), and stabilising credit costs around 2.6–3.0%. Management has been consistent in prioritising risk-adjusted returns over headline growth, evidenced by calibrated MFI exposure, conservative provisioning, and disciplined MSME expansion. Fee-based and technology-led credit solutions remain a structural differentiator, though monetisation is still early-stage. Overall, execution credibility has improved as guidance on growth, margins, and credit costs has largely aligned with delivery by Q3FY26.

evidence: Q1FY26: Management acknowledged FY25 headwinds and stated that 'residual impact of FY25 stress will linger through the first half of the year' but set clear recovery expectations for H2.
Q2FY26: Management explicitly reiterated credit cost guidance of 2.6–2.8% and AUM growth of 20–22%, signalling confidence without over-promising.
Q3FY26: CEO stated 'incremental PAR 0+ accretion has reverted to pre-stress level' and backed it with vintage and guardrail data, reflecting higher specificity.
Q4FY25: Management openly discussed one-time DLG provisioning and management overlay, clearly separating accounting prudence from underlying business performance.

guidance_vs_delivery.what_was_promised: H2FY26 credit cost to moderate to 2.7–2.9% and AUM growth to re-accelerate
guidance_vs_delivery.what_was_delivered: By Q2FY26, credit cost improved to 2.7% and AUM growth reached 15% YoY with momentum picking up

guidance_vs_delivery.what_was_promised: Full-year FY26 credit cost of ~2.6–2.8% and ROA ~2.8%
guidance_vs_delivery.what_was_delivered: Q3FY26 exit credit cost guided at 2.7–3.0% and ROA improved to 2.7%

timeline.what_was_said: Credit costs elevated due to MFI stress; provisioning increased prudently.
Ex-DLG credit cost would have been ~2.6%.
Exit credit cost expected to remain within 2.7–3.0%.

topics.assessment: Management steadily guided and delivered a normalisation path without sharp reversals.

timeline.what_was_said: Target to increase D2C mix to ~70% by FY28.

topics.assessment: Clear execution against a multi-year stated objective.

guidance_evolution.pattern_summary: Management guidance has been realistic, conservative, and largely unchanged over time, with delivery improving visibility and credibility.

margin_commentary: Margins have been discussed primarily through a risk-adjusted lens rather than headline NIM. Management consistently cited mix shift towards D2C, declining cost of funds, and fee income as key levers. NIM improved from ~9.1% in FY25 to ~9.9% in Q3FY26, supported by ~90 bps YoY reduction in cost of funds. Margin guidance has remained credible, with no abrupt reversals.
revenue_growth_narrative: Revenue growth has been positioned as a combination of balance-sheet-led lending (MSME, consumer) and capital-light fee income (placements, funds, tech platforms). While FY25 growth was muted by MFI stress, FY26 saw revival led by MSME (+40%+ YoY) and consumer finance. The narrative around growth drivers has remained consistent, with no sudden pivots.
key_risks_flagged_by_management: MFI over-leveraging and borrower stress (Q2FY25, Q4FY25)
Stress in unsecured small-ticket MSME loans (Q3FY26)
Lag in transmission of repo rate cuts to MCLR affecting liquidity (Q1FY26, Q3FY26)
positive_signals: PAR 0+ accretion in MFI turned negative sequentially (Q3FY26)
Cost of funds declined ~90 bps YoY to 8.5% (Q3FY26)
Fee income grew ~50% YoY driven by placements (Q3FY26)
red_flags: Repeated need for management overlays and one-time provisions in FY25 raised questions on initial risk calibration.
Intermediate retail credit cost volatility attributed to 'prudence' rather than specific asset issues, limiting transparency.

business_problems_and_challenges.problem: Delayed transmission of policy rate cuts into effective borrowing costs, impacting near-term margin expansion.
business_problems_and_challenges.evidence: Management noted that despite 125 bps repo cuts, MCLR reduction was only ~25–30 bps (Q3FY26).

business_problems_and_challenges.problem: High operational intensity required for MSME collections and underwriting due to physical branch-led model.
business_problems_and_challenges.evidence: Management highlighted addition of sales and collection staff and branch expansion to support MSME growth (Q2FY26, Q3FY26).

overall_investment_signal: positive: Improving execution, stabilised asset quality, and credible delivery against guidance outweigh residual sectoral risks.

revenue_targets.basis: D2C growth momentum and MSME expansion

earnings_guidance.basis: Margin expansion and stabilised credit cost

market_landscape.addressable_market: Indian retail credit market ~₹75 trillion growing at 16–18% CAGR (Q2FY25)
market_landscape.competitive_position: Differentiated by integrated credit solutions, proprietary tech, and fee franchise
market_landscape.government_policy_tailwinds: RBI rate cuts, GST reductions, MFIN guardrails
market_landscape.government_policy_headwinds: Digital lending and MFI regulatory tightening (FY25)

cyclicality_and_macro_factors.interest_rate_impact: Declining rates improve margins with lag (Q1FY26–Q3FY26)
